items.title: [Bug] Four implemented loss layers skip `loss_scale` in `calcDerivative`
items.body:
## Summary

On current `main` (`a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258`), four
implemented loss derivatives do not apply the `RunLayerContext` loss scale:

- `CrossEntropySigmoidLossLayer`;
- `CrossEntropySoftmaxLossLayer`;
- `KLDLossLayer`;
- `ConstantDerivativeLossLayer`.

`MSELossLayer` does call `LossLayer::applyLossScale`, and the mixed-precision
optimizer path later divides FP32 gradients by the same scale. This makes the
loss-layer behavior inconsistent and can reduce the effective gradient by the
scale factor after unscaling.

## Minimal runtime reproduction

I constructed real `Var_Grad` objects and a real `RunLayerContext` with
`loss_scale=8`, then called the production `calcDerivative` methods.

| Layer | Base derivative | Expected | Observed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| sigmoid cross-entropy, `z=0`, label `1` | `-0.5` | `-4.0` | `-0.5` |
| softmax cross-entropy, logits `[0,0]`, label `[1,0]` | `[-0.5,0.5]` | `[-4,4]` | `[-0.5,0.5]` |
| KLD, `P=0.25`, `Q=0.5` | `-0.5` | `-4.0` | `-0.5` |
| constant derivative | `1.0` | `8.0` | `1.0` |

The KLD check was run after locally applying the label-mutation correction
reported in #4328, so that separate defect does not explain this result.

## Minimal fix

Call the existing helper after each derivative is formed:

```cpp
LossLayer::applyLossScale(context, ret_derivative);
```

For KLD the destination tensor is named `deriv`, so the call is:

```cpp
LossLayer::applyLossScale(context, deriv);
```

## Verification

Before the fix, all four focused checks fail with the values above. After the
four helper calls:

```text
loss-scale counterexamples: 4/4 passed
focused loss regression:   71/71 passed
```

The focused regression filter covers both new loss-scale suites, the existing
`LossCross/LayerSemantics` parameterization, and the KLD repeatability test.

I can submit the tests and the four-call patch as a PR if this interpretation
of the `loss_scale` contract matches the maintainers' intent.

items.title: [ Wait for #4306, #4308, #4313 ] [layers][engine] Promote the LLM layers into the core, and open registration to any engine
items.body:
Five layer classes that are pure shape-and-orchestration have lived inside the
CausalLM application as per-layer plugin `shared_library` objects: `qkv_layer`,
`lm_head`, `logit_softcapping`, `scalar_multiply` and `tie_word_embedding`.
None of them names a backend. Any other application that wanted one had to copy
it, and no accelerator context could register it at all, so `createLayer()`
threw for those types under `engine=gpu` and `engine=cuda`: a language model
could not build its graph there whatever the rest of the graph could run on.

This promotes all five into `nntrainer/layers/llm/`, the home this series opened
for backend-neutral layers that belong to the language-model vocabulary but
carry no `LayerType` identity. Like `layers/loss/` they compile straight into
libnntrainer instead of being built as plugin objects, and they register under a
string key only, which is what lets the cpu, OpenCL and CUDA contexts register
the very same C++ class under the very same name.

They are genuine renames -- five classes, ten files, R67-R98 similarity, all ten
detected as renames by `git diff -M` against the base branch -- so the
review is the small delta on each, not a thousand-line re-read.

The application's SwiGLU fork is folded into the neutral `SwiGLULayer` at the
same time. There were two SwiGLU layers computing `silu(gate) * up` under the
type string `swiglu`, and which one a graph got depended on its engine. The core
class absorbs the fork's `SkipPrefill` property, its
`updateTensorsByInputDimensions`, and a corrected row window: the old code
passed `batch*channel*height` rows on every incremental call, which is the whole
buffer rather than the live rows.

Two further gaps close here. `Context::registerLayerFactory` -- the non-template
seam that lets a caller register a layer on any backend without `static_cast`-ing
the resolved `Context` down to a concrete class -- was overridden by `AppContext`
and `ClContext` but not by `CudaContext`, which inherited the base refusal and
reported `-1` for a context that does have a registry. And `ComputeOps` declares
`mean_rows` and `l2_normalize_rows`, which the CPU table implements and
`CudaComputeOps` inherits, but `ClComputeOps` derives from the bare `ComputeOps`
whose entries throw: the sentence-embedding tail did not fall back on a
gpu-context tensor, it failed. This adds the OpenCL column for both.

Deletions exceed the promoted-code size because the application forks go away in
the same change: exactly one copy of each layer exists in the tree afterwards,
and the app-side originals are gone.

**Not here, deliberately.** GeGLU is not in this PR -- it is created directly at
`nntrainer/layers/llm/` by #4304, because `cl_context.cpp` includes and registers
it at an earlier rung than this one. The fused sigmoid-gate layer family is
excluded from the series, as it was from #4313: no in-tree model reaches those
ops. No concrete layer header is added to `nntrainer_headers`, matching every
other concrete layer header in the tree, so nothing new is installed and the
RPM/deb packaging surface is unchanged.

**Verification.** Built with `-Denable-test=true -Denable-transformer=true`.
CPU: `meson test` 43/43 Ok, 0 Fail; `unittest_layers` 1023/1023;
`unittest_nntrainer_appcontext` 32/32; `unittest_causallm_models` 79 run,
67 pass, 12 skip, 0 fail -- that last one is the gate for a change that moves
five layers across a library boundary and shifts every app model's includes.
The OpenCL configuration has zero object-compile failures and exactly the same
pre-existing CLBlast executable-link count as its base branch.
`clang-format-diff` over this PR's own range returns 0 lines.

items.title: [engine] Open the backend registry + neutral device-capability probe
items.body:
Groundwork so a compute backend (OpenCL/CUDA/NPU) can register itself and
advertise its capabilities without the core needing a compile-time enum edit or
a static_cast to a concrete Context subtype. No behavior change: every new seam
is either a default that reproduces today's path or an inert tag nothing reads
yet.

Registry (T3):
- Context gains a non-template registerLayerFactory(PtrFactoryType<Layer>, key,
  int_key) virtual (base returns -1 "unsupported"); AppContext overrides it to
  forward to the existing per-class registerFactory<Layer>. Engine gains a
  registerLayerFactory(engine_name, ...) facade that resolves the target Context
  by name via getRegisteredContext() and dispatches to it — so a backend or the
  app can register a factory into a specific backend without a static_cast.
- The `engine=` layer property changes from a closed EnumProperty
  (ComputeEngineTypeInfo) to a registry-open Property<std::string>:
  LayerNode::compute_engine is now the context NAME, normalized against the live
  registry in Engine::parseComputeEngine (unknown/unavailable -> "cpu" fallback,
  matching what createLayerObject already resolved). getComputeEngineType()
  still returns the name string (unchanged return type), so existing callers
  (network_graph, neuralnet) are untouched. A CUDA row is added to the enum
  table for the compat setter, and toLayerComputeEngine() maps a registered name
  back to the residency-plane enum via the new Context::residencyEngine()
  (base=CPU) instead of the central name->enum string table.

Device capabilities (T1):
- A backend-neutral DeviceCaps POD (backend/arch/vendor/unified_memory/subgroups/
  compute_units/max_alloc/... — no cl_mem/CUDA types) with a one-line toString(),
  exposed via a Context::caps() virtual (base returns a default CPU snapshot).
  AppContext::initialize() logs it once. Log-only: no decision site reads it.

Tag threading (inert foundation):
- TensorSpecV2 gains engine (producing layer's LayerComputeEngine, default CPU)
  and a TensorRole hint (default GENERIC); InitLayerContext stamps the layer's
  engine onto its output specs at the single outSpec() chokepoint;
  RunLayerContext carries a run_engine. Nothing consumes these yet (the residency
  resolver that will is a later change), so output/allocation is byte-identical.

The per-backend concrete overrides (ClContext/CudaContext caps()/residencyEngine
probing), the ExecPlan resolver that will consume DeviceCaps, and the
TensorPool residency-class derivation that will consume the engine tag are each
deferred to their own follow-up changes; this one only lands the neutral base.

Depends-on: the ComputeOps whole-op dispatch change ("[cpu_backend] Add whole-op
ComputeOps dispatch surface + CPU baseline") — must merge first.

Verified with a gcc-13 -Werror plain build (enable-fp16=false, enable-test=true)
and the regression suite: unittest_nntrainer_appcontext (12),
unittest_nntrainer_models (125), unittest_models (156), unittest_layers (1020),
unittest_nntrainer_cpu_backend (53), unittest_nntrainer_tensor (267),
unittest_compiler (38), unittest_nntrainer_graph (12) all pass.

Repro:
  meson setup build -Denable-transformer=true -Denable-test=true \
    -Denable-tflite-interpreter=false -Denable-tflite-backbone=false \
    -Denable-fp16=false --buildtype=plain
  ninja -C build
  meson test -C build unittest_nntrainer_appcontext unittest_nntrainer_graph

items.title: [tflite] Support Tensorflow Lite Selected Ops in nntrainer
items.body:
we will update tensorflow lite package for support tensorflow lite selected ops 

below is temp solution for using them 
## Build Tensorflow lite .so file with selected ops 

Requirements
  gcc, g++, glibc

1. Download Tensorflow, Flatbuffer
 ```.sh
$ wget https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/archive/refs/tags/v2.11.0.tar.gz 
$ wget https://github.com/google/flatbuffers/archive/refs/tags/v22.11.23.tar.gz
```

2. unzip tar.gz files 
```.sh
$ tar -zxvf {filename}
```

3. Add this dependency to /tensorflow/lite/BUILD →  tflite_cc_shared_object 
```.BUILD
→(remove this line) "//tensorflow/lite/kernels:builtin_ops_all_linked",
"//tensorflow/lite/kernels:builtin_ops",
"//tensorflow/lite/delegates/flex:delegate",
"//tensorflow/lite/delegates/flex:exported_symbols.lds",
"//tensorflow/lite/delegates/flex:version_script.lds",
```

4. Download dependency
```.sh
$ sudo apt install python3-dev python3-pip
$ pip install pip numpy wheel packaging requests opt_einsum
$ pip install keras_preprocessing --no-deps
$ sudo apt-get install gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu
```

5. install bazelisk
```.sh
$ sudo apt install npm
$ sudo npm install -g @bazel/bazelisk 
$ bazelisk 
```
**for x86_64**

```.sh
$ bazelisk build --config=monolithic --config=noaws --config=nogcp --config=nohdfs --config=nonccl  --fat_apk_cpu=x86,x86_64  --experimental_ui_max_stdouterr_bytes=1073741819 -c opt //tensorflow/lite:libtensorflowlite.so
```

**for aarch64**

You need to hide the system's openssl library. For this go to usr/include  folder and make sudo mv openssl openssl.original. 

```.sh
$ bazelisk build --config=monolithic --config=noaws --config=nogcp --config=nohdfs --config=nonccl --config=elinux_aarch64 --experimental_ui_max_stdouterr_bytes=1073741819 -c opt //tensorflow/lite:libtensorflowlite.so
```

## Apply to local environments

1. update "/usr/lib/pkgconfig/tensorflow2-lite.pc" file -- update like below
```.txt
    Name: tensorflow lite
    Description: tensorflow lite static library
    Version: 2.11.0
    Libs: -L/usr/lib -ltensorflowlite
    Cflags: -I/usr/include/tensorflowlite
```
2. move libtensorflowlite.so file to /usr/lib
 
3. make dir in /usr/include as name "tensorflowlite"

4. in /usr/include/tensorflowlite put flatbuffer and tensorflow (it come from github)

6. in nntrainer meson build -> ninja install again

7. in your app (you can run)

summary : just change pkgconfig file and make them to use new .so file we can run Simpleshot nntrainer Application 

I test this method on my local PC (Ubuntu 22.04, x86_64)
